items.title: Tamil Nadu police step-up surveillance on habitual offenders
points: The Tamil Nadu police have arrested 443 accused persons involved in various crimes, including drug offences and violent crimes, across the State and enhanced vigil on habitual offenders.

Police personnel checked the activities of more than 15,000 anti-social elements and thousands of vehicles as part of the operation, which resulted in the arrest of 443 suspects who were produced in local courts and remanded in judicial custody.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Director-General of Police and Head of the Police Force, Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, said the two-day operation was planned decisively to curb criminal activities, disrupt drug distribution networks, and reinforce absolute…
Police teams across Tamil Nadu systematically tracked and checked 8,626 listed rowdies.
As many as 796 habitual offenders were placed under strict preventive surveillance.

To prevent retaliatory crimes and maintain public peace, Dr Aggarwal said the police stepped up surveillance on 2,924 accused individuals previously involved in murder and assault cases, including those recently released from prison.

items.title: Keralam at 70: holding a mirror to India
points: ‘The 16th Keralam Assembly has 51% Hindu, 25% Muslim, and 24% Christian MLAs roughly corresponding to their populations.
Such consociationalism is rare, even globally’ | Photo Credit: X/@vdsatheesan via ANI In 1956, Keralam was amongst the poorest States, on par with Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

Presently, it is amongst the richest; but more importantly, it has a lower infant mortality than the U.S. If Keralam were counted as a nation, it would rank 75 on the Human Development Index, ahead of China.
It would also be 55 ranks above India which is at 130.
This transformation and divergence from the national path is the globally lauded ‘Keralam story’.
Keralam reinforces Amartya Sen’s original thesis that development is about expanding human freedoms rather than mere economic growth; human development does not require high incomes.
Yet even now the central thrust of the national development regime is “Viksit Bharat 2047,” an income-based development measure.

items.title: Recent repairs on OMR come undone
points: Portions of Rajiv Gandhi Salai (OMR) and the Medavakkam - Sholinganallur Road continue to have bad patches and potholes that making driving on these roads difficult.
These are sections where the Chennai Metrorail works are under way.
Raman said the worst spot was the Sholinganallur junction.
This leads to traffic slowing down considerably.
Repairs undertaken recently seen to have come undone, said Krishna Suresh, a resident of Karapakkam.
“A lot of small-sized blue metal have come loose from both the OMR and the Medavakkam - Sholinganallur Road.
Co-founder of Federation of OMR Residents Associations Harsha Koda said that portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have only fallen apart.

items.title: Tasmac introduces three year transfer norm for shop employees
points: VELANKANNI RAJ The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) is set to reshuffle employees across its retail network in Tamil Nadu, deploying staff at outlets based on manpower requirements.
Under a new Transfer and Posting Policy for Tasmac liquor Retail Vending Shop Personnel, 2026, the state run liquor retailer has proposed transferring employees across shops once every three years.
Outlets with average monthly sales of ₹10 lakh and above will be classified as Category A and will have a minimum workforce of nine employees.
Those with sales of more than ₹5 lakh but less than ₹10 lakh will fall under Category B, with a workforce of eight employees.
Outlets recording sales of less than ₹5 lakh will be classified as Category C and will have five employees.
Employees who have complete three years at a shop as on November 1 will be considered for the transfer.

items.title: UPI Charges After Diwali: Will Shops Start Charging You Extra From Nov 9?
points: NPCI’s UPI and Services Steering Committee decided on October 13, 2026, to defer the rollout of the new Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) until after Diwali, citing the festive season.
With Diwali falling on November 8 this year, the revised implementation window has arrived, although NPCI has yet to announce an exact date.
The charge applies to eligible bank-account-funded UPI payments made by customers to merchants for transactions above ₹2,000.
Standard merchants will pay an MDR of 0.4%, capped at ₹300 per transaction once the payment reaches ₹75,000.
For example, a ₹3,000 payment would attract a ₹12 merchant fee, while a ₹50,000 payment would cost the merchant ₹200.
Certain essential and thin-margin categories, including railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs, will pay a flat ₹5.
Capital-market transactions involving mutual funds, securities and stockbrokers will attract an MDR of 0.02%, also capped at ₹300.
The following transactions remain free: NPCI and the Finance Ministry have stated that payments of ₹2,000 or less account for most P2M transaction volume.

items.title: Soybeans, corn rally after USDA pegs US harvest, stocks below expectations
points: Corn futures also rallied as the USDA cut its US production and stocks forecasts by more than expected.
Wheat futures followed corn and soybeans higher, though gains were limited by expectations for larger global supplies due to big crops in the southern hemisphere.
The USDA surprised traders last month by raising its US corn harvest outlook despite adverse weather in parts of the Midwest this summer while also forecasting a record-large soybean crop.
The USDA's US soy production forecast on Tuesday was 23 million bushels below the average analyst estimate in a Reuters poll.
The USDA lowered its US corn harvest and end-of-season stocks forecasts by more than expected, although its outlook for South America's harvest increased.
Chicago Board of Trade January soybean futures were 39-1/2 cents higher at $12.27-3/4 a bushel at 12:25 p.m.
December corn rebounded from a four-month low on Monday to $4.50-1/2 a bushel, up 11-1/4 cents.

items.title: Two persons killed in separate road incidents
points: Two persons were killed in separate road incidents near Kilpennathur and Arcot towns in Tiruvannamalai and Ranipet districts respectively on Tuesday.

Initial inquiry revealed that Nandakumar, a private school staff, was on his way to school on the Chennai – Bengaluru Highway (NH 48) when a private bus hit the two-wheeler he was riding at Melvisharam in Ranipet.
Passersby rushed a badly injured Nandakumar to Government Taluk Hospital in Arcot town, where doctors said that he was brought dead.
A case was registered and a probe is under way.
In a separate incident, the victim, Venkatesan was riding his autorickshaw from a petrol pump towards the Chittoor – Cuddalore Highway at Kilpennathur, when a car rammed the autorickshaw.
The police said in the impact, Venkatesan died on the spot.
On being informed, Kilpennathur police inspected the spot and a case was registered.

items.title: Over 74 lakh voters missing from Tamil Nadu electoral rolls, says citizens’ collective
points: Political economist Parakala Prabhakar speaking at a press conference in Chennai on Tuesday.
RAGU The Independent Young Citizens Collective (IYCC) has alleged that 74.07 lakh voters have been removed from Tamil Nadu’s electoral rolls and demanded an inquiry into the alleged deletions.

Announcing a rally on Anna Salai on November 26, as part of a nationwide day of action against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the collective said the reported deletion of such a large number of names has raised serious questions…

Ms. Radhika Ganesh alleged that the SIR was a BJP-RSS project without constitutional basis and claimed that it had resulted in the removal of 74.07 lakh voters, accounting for around 11.5% of the State’s electorate.

She described the deletions as a democratic crisis and sought answers from the Election Commission of India, accountability from the Union government and a clear response from political parties in Tamil Nadu.

items.title: Govardhan puja, Gau puja celebrated at Hare Krishna Vaikuntham
points: Govardhan puja and Gau puja were held at the Sri Sri Radha Madan Mohan temple at Hare Krishna Vaikuntham, Gambheeram, Visakhapatnam, on Tuesday.
The celebrations began with a palanquin procession of the deities from the temple to the goshala, where the cows were worshipped.
Niskinchana Bhakta Dasa, president of the Hare Krishna Movement, Visakhapatnam, spoke about the significance of Lord Krishna’s Govardhan Leela and Gau puja.
Devotees prepared a traditional Annakuta, a mountain-like offering comprising 108 varieties of vegetarian food for Lord Krishna.
They also performed govardhan parikrama (walking around) the offering.
The programme included damodara aarti and the offering of ghee lamps to the deity.

points: Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said the central bank needs at least two more quarter-point rate increases to curb persistent inflation and prevent price pressures from becoming entrenched.

items.title: Woman, son die after being found injured at home in Mattannur
points: A 56-year-old woman and her 21-year-old son died on Tuesday (November 10) after they were found with serious wounds at their home in Mattannur.
The deceased were identified as Jyothi and Naveen Krishna.

Jyothi’s husband, Jayakrishnan, reportedly found them lying in a pool of blood on the second floor of their house on Lions Club Road when he returned home after visiting Mattannur town around 9.30 a.m.
The police and residents rushed to the house and took the two to the hospital.
The police said both were in an extremely critical condition on the way to the hospital.
The Mattannur police have registered a case and stepped up the investigation.

items.title: Performance Shipping Inc. Announces $4.0 Million Share Buyback Plan
points: Performance Shipping Inc. , a global shipping company specializing in the ownership of tanker vessels, announced today that its Board of Directors has approved a share repurchase plan (the “Plan”).
Under the Plan, the Company may repurchase up to $4.0 million of its outstanding common shares.

The Company may repurchase common shares pursuant to Rule 10b-18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, or pursuant to a trading plan adopted in accordance with Rule 10b5‐1 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

The Plan may be suspended, terminated, or modified at any time for any reason, including market conditions, the cost of repurchasing shares, the availability of alternative investment opportunities, liquidity, and other factors deemed appropriate.
These factors may also affect the timing and amount of share repurchases.
The Plan does not obligate the Company to purchase any of its shares under the Plan.
The Board of Directors’ authorization of the Plan is effective immediately and expires on June 30, 2027.

items.title: Yangzijiang Shipbuilding’s order-wins exceed target by 55%
points: Mainboard-listed Yangzijiang (YZJ) Shipbuilding has announced a strong year for orderbook wins in its 3QFY2026 business update.
At the ten-month mark, the company has secured US$6.98 ($8.92) billion in year-to-date order wins.
This is 55% higher than its FY2026 target of US$4.5 billion.
In total, YZJ Shipbuilding’s orderbook stood at US$26.3 billion as at Oct 31, with deliveries slated up to 2030.
Around two-third of its orderbook value comprises clean energy newbuild vessels.
YZJ Shipbuilding executive chairman Ren Letian says that the company made “strong” progress in securing new orders.
“This was underpinned by contracts for ultra-large LNG dual-fuel containerships and large bulk carriers,” he adds.
“With delivery slots across the industry largely committed through 2029, we remain selective, prioritising vessel types and contract terms that preserve the quality of our orderbook,” he remarks.

items.title: China extends suspension of US ship port charges until January
points: China will continue to suspend special port charges on US-linked ships until Jan.
10, 2027, the Ministry of Transport said on Nov.
9, as Beijing and Washington maintain a temporary truce amid an ongoing US-China trade dispute.
9, saying the decision, with State Council approval, was made to implement the outcome of a recent round of China-US trade talks.
The latest Chinese extension came after the US Trade Representative proposed keeping its port charges against Chinese ships suspended for a further two months through Jan.

China introduced the special port fees in October 2025 on ships built, flagged in the US or at least 25% owned by US entities, in retaliation for US Section 301 measures targeting China’s maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors.
The US measures included port service fees on Chinese-owned and operated ships, as well as China-built vessels calling at US ports.

items.title: US Dollar Credit Supply: October slowdown
points: Drop in supply in October, but Reverse Yankee supply continues to impress USD corporate issuance totalled US$59bn in October, down from US$112bn in September.
Despite the slower monthly volume, YTD issuance reached US$1,059bn, exceeding last year’s full-year level of US$920bn.
Corporate net supply remained positive at US$30bn in October, bringing the YTD total to US$601bn.
TMT remained the largest contributor to USD corporate supply, with US$30bn issued in October and YTD issuance reaching US$435bn, compared with US$208bn over the same period in 2025.
Utilities and Industrials & Chemicals remained the next largest issuing sectors, with YTD volumes of US$165bn and US$131bn respectively.
Corporate Reverse Yankee issuance amounted to €6.8bn in October, lifting YTD volume to €104bn.
Bank bond supply slowed down in October, but YTD levels remain ahead of 2025 USD bank bond supply reached just over US$52bn in October, down US$18bn from September’s level.
Despite the recent slowdown, USD-denominated covered bond supply stands at nearly US$24bn in 2026 YTD, up US$13bn YoY.

items.title: Fed’s Waller says larger hike should be considered if October CPI runs hot
points: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Tuesday he would support a 25-basis-point interest rate hike in December even if October inflation improves, and that a larger 50-basis-point move should be considered if price pressures stay strong.
Speaking in London hours before the release of October consumer price index data, Waller said the U.S. economy is growing strongly and the labor market is stable, but inflation remains too high.
“While I am hoping for an improvement over September, even if this occurs, I would still support a 25 basis point increase in the FOMC’s policy rate at our December meeting,” he said.
September’s inflation data were bad,” he said.
He noted that the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge rose 3.7% over the past year in September, while the core measure, which strips out food and energy, rose 3.1%.
If October core CPI comes in around 0.3% for the month or higher, similar to the previous two readings, Waller said the Fed should consider a 50 basis point hike in December.

items.title: US Inflation Slows Down
points: US consumer inflation moderated in October, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising 0.4% month on month after a 0.6% increase in September.

Shelter costs climbed 0.3%, accounting for more than 30% of the overall monthly increase, while core inflation, excluding food and energy, also rose 0.3%, matching the pace recorded in August and September.
Food prices increased 0.5%, driven by higher grocery costs, particularly snacks, meat, fruit and vegetables, and dairy products.
Prices for meals away from home also advanced 0.5%.
Energy prices rose 0.7%, slowing sharply from September’s 5.2% increase, as a 1% rise in gasoline and a 0.9% gain in electricity costs were partly offset by lower natural gas prices.
Recreation, medical care and motor vehicle insurance also became more expensive, while used cars and communication costs declined.
The BLS said it could not calculate annual inflation rates for October because data for October 2025 were unavailable due to a government funding lapse.

items.title: Greece Inflation Rate Climbs to Highest Since 2023
points: The annual inflation rate in Greece rose to 5.7% in October 2026, its highest level since February 2023, up from 5% in September.
Inflation accelerated in housing and utilities (15.1% vs 14.7%), transportation (13.8% vs 11.3%), recreation and culture (2.1% vs 1.6%), and clothing and footwear (3.8% vs 0.3%).
Meanwhile, price growth stood at 2.9% for education and 3.5% for insurance and financial services.
By contrast, inflation moderated for furnishings and household equipment (0.4% vs 0.6%) and restaurants and hotels (5.8% vs 6.9%).
Prices fell further for information and communication (-2.2% vs -1.9%), while alcoholic beverages and tobacco moved into deflation (-0.2% vs 0%).
From the previous month, consumer prices rose by 0.7% in October, slowing from a 2.1% increase in September.

items.title: Greece Industrial Output Rebounds Sharply in August
points: Industrial output in Greece rose 5.8% year-on-year in August 2026, rebounding from a revised 1.1% decline in the previous month and highest recorded growth since March 2026.
The recovery was led by electricity supply, which surged by 13.2%, reversing a 12.4% contraction in the previous month.

Manufacturing growth also strengthened to 4.0% from 2.0% in July, supported by robust gains in motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers (269.1%), repair and installation of machinery and equipment (27.8%), textiles (15.6%), and other transport equipment…
Conversely, wearing apparel (-18.4%), machinery and equipment not elsewhere classified (-6.7%), and basic metals (-4.8%) recorded the steepest declines.
Mining and quarrying rebounded (1.5% vs -3.5%), while water supply declined at slower pace (2.5% vs 4.0%).
On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, industrial activity rose 2.0% from -1.8% in the previous month.

points: Chandragiri TDP MLA Pulivarthi Nani and TUDA chairman C.
Of the 35 Zilla Parishat Territorial Constituencies (ZPTC), the TDP won 25—21 in the elections and four unanimously.
In the Mandal Parishat Territorial Constituencies (MPTC) elections, the TDP won 185 in the elections and 125 unanimously, taking its total to 310.
The Jana Sena and BJP won 12 and eight respectively in the elections, apart from winning nine and five seats unanimously, taking the alliance total to 344.

items.title: T.N. government invites tenders for coverage of Assembly proceedings for two years
points: The Assembly proceedings have been telecast live since the TVK-led government assumed office. | Photo Credit: B.
JOTHI RAMALINGAM The Tamil Nadu government has invited tenders for complete coverage of Assembly proceedings for from January 2027 to December 2028.

According to the tender document, the work includes recording the entire session using a multi-camera setup, editing and other post-production work, and handing over the footage to the Assembly authorities for immediate telecast on satellite television…
The contract will cover 80 days of Assembly proceedings a year.

Sign language interpretation and captions in Tamil and English, indicating the name and constituency of the Member speaking and the item of business being discussed, are also part of the post-production work.
“Unless directed otherwise, the cameras shall show the Chair and the Member called to speak.
The footage can be edited only to remove expunged portions based on the direction of Assembly authorities, adjournment breaks, and technical faults.
The Assembly proceedings have been telecast live since the TVK-led government assumed office.

items.title: Nvidia sell-off deepens, fall 6.3%; wipes $10 billion off Jensen Huang's wealth, slips to 12th on Forbes rich list
points: Nvidia shares came under another round of selling pressure in Tuesday's trade, falling 6.3% to hit a seven-month low of $166.5 apiece, following a 4.3% decline in the previous session.

Investors appeared concerned about the chip giant's future prospects amid reports surrounding CEO Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who has reportedly been identified as a Chinese intelligence asset.

The latest crash in Nvidia shares has dealt a major blow to Jensen Huang's net worth, which is on track to decline by another $10 billion to $145.6 billion from $154 billion at the previous close, according to Forbes.
This followed a $7.4 billion decline on Monday, pushing him down to 12th place in Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires ranking, according to the publication's data.
He owns more than 3.5% of Nvidia, which he took public in 1999.

Under Huang's leadership, Nvidia's GPUs first became dominant in computer gaming and later emerged as a critical technology in artificial intelligence, propelling the company's market capitalisation past $5 trillion in 2025.

items.title: AR Rahman's Gurugram concert postponed over ‘unforeseen circumstances’, rescheduled for next year
points: Two-time Oscar-winning composer AR Rahman’s concert in Gurugram on November 21, which was part of his ongoing Wonderment Tour, has been postponed and rescheduled to next year.
The concert was originally scheduled for next week on November 21, and was to take place at 7 pm at Backyard Sports Club in Gurugram.
Nidhi Sharma, a resident of Gurugram who had purchased premium tickets for the concert, expressed disappointment over the postponement.
Meanwhile, this is not the first time the Grammy Award-winning composer's concert has faced last-minute cancellations.
Last year, several tickets for his concert, titled ‘AR Rahman: Harmony of Hearts’, were abruptly cancelled just 24 hours before the scheduled show.

items.title: Patna Civic Body Raises Rs 200 Crore Via Bonds, Gets Listed On Stock Exchange
points: The Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC) has raised nearly Rs 200 crore through municipal bonds, becoming the first urban local body in Bihar to have its bonds listed on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The bond issue had a base size of approximately Rs 100.03 crore.
Bidding was conducted on October 30 through the NSE's electronic platform, attracting investor demand exceeding Rs 205 crore.
Following the strong response, the issue size was increased to nearly Rs 200 crore, enabling the corporation to raise Rs 199.99 crore.
The estimated cost of the projects is Rs 270.45 crore.
While approximately Rs 200 crore will come from the bond proceeds, the remaining amount will be met from the corporation's internal resources.
He described the expansion of the bond issue from its initial size of around Rs 100 crore to nearly Rs 200 crore as a significant achievement.

items.title: 51 Years Later, the Edmund Fitzgerald and Her 29 Lost Mariners Are Remembered
points: The SS Edmund Fitzgerald underway on the Great Lakes.
The 729-foot freighter sank in Lake Superior on November 10, 1975, with the loss of all 29 crew members.

(Photo: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers) Fifty-one years ago today, the SS Edmund Fitzgerald disappeared beneath the waters of Lake Superior during a powerful November storm, taking all 29 crew members with her in one of the most enduring tragedies in Great…
The 729-foot freighter sank on November 10, 1975, about 17 miles north-northwest of Whitefish Point, Michigan.
On Tuesday, the Great Lakes Shipwreck Historical Society will mark the 51st anniversary with a private memorial ceremony for surviving family members and others connected to the ship and its crew.

The Edmund Fitzgerald was among the largest and best-known freighters operating on the Great Lakes when she departed Superior, Wisconsin, on November 9, 1975, carrying more than 26,000 long tons of taconite iron ore pellets bound for Detroit.

Hapag-Lloyd and Inmarsat Maritime: a case study in connected shipping
points: Hapag-Lloyd, the world’s fifth-largest container carrier, operates 300 vessels on 133 liner services, transporting 13.5 million twenty-foot-equivalent units a year between 600 ports worldwide.

According to Patrick Briest, Hapag-Lloyd’s Senior Director of Operations and IT Products,digitalisation “can do many things”, but making things simpler – from both a commercial and operational perspective – is its one “superpower”.
“We don’t digitalise just because we can,” Briest told the audience at a recent Inmarsat ‘Connected to Perform’ seminar during SMM 2026.

Digitalisation and connectivity, then, enable shipping companies like Hapag-Lloyd to make smarter operational decisions based on a richer and more immediate view of what is happening on the vessel and across the network.

Whereas ships previously operated as isolated assets, they increasingly function as an extension of head office, with seafarers and shorestaff working as one team, and the Atlantic Ocean – in Briest’s words – becoming “as connected as downtown Frankfurt”.

items.title: Gurugram traffic policemen, homeguards to be transferred every 60 days after Diwali 'gift' demand leads to crackdown
points: After a home guard was arrested for allegedly demanding "Diwali gifts" from a motorist in Gurugram, Police Commissioner Sibash Kabiraj has issued a series of instructions for traffic policemen and home guards to minimise the possibilities of irregularities…
According to officials on Tuesday, random transfers will be carried out among the Gurugram traffic personnel every 60 days through an automated computerised system.

Zonal Officer (ZO) and Traffic Inspector (TI) will be held accountable if any traffic police personnel, home guard or special police officer is found involved in corrupt practices while performing traffic duty, they added.
The home guard incident took place on November 7, when a vlogger was travelling with his family in Gurugram.
He was signalled by a home guard to pull over the car near Cyber Hub, and the latter repeatedly wished them "Happy Diwali".
The accused home guard then allegedly began indirectly soliciting money or "gifts", saying it had been a "dry Diwali".

items.title: Suvendu Adhikari Visits Kali Puja Of Mamata Banerjee's Estranged brother
points: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari walked into the backyard of his predecessor Mamata Banerjee today, visiting a Kali Puja organised by her brother Babun Banerjee.
The spot was just two houses away from Mamata Banerjee's residence in Kalighat.
The former Chief Minister's door remained shut while he received a warm welcome at her brother's puja.
Babun Banerjee touched Adhikari's feet, garlanded him and declared his support for the Chief Minister.
The Kali Puja was organised by Mamata Banerjee's brother.
The optics today were stark - Adhikari walking past Mamata Banerjee's house - the hub of power for a decade -- and getting a warm welcome from her brother.
Then in presence of Babun Banerjee and his family, he offered prayers and performed aarti before the idol of Goddess Kali.
"Looking at what Suvendu Adhikari has done for Bengal in last six months, want see him become Chief Minister again," he added.

items.title: India, US discuss customs and trade facilitation as both sides push for early bilateral deal
points: A team of US officials visited India earlier this month for talks on the proposed bilateral trade agreement (BTA) as New Delhi and Washington remain engaged for an early conclusion of the first tranche of the deal, an official said on Tuesday.
The two sides discussed issues pertaining to customs and trade facilitation last week in New Delhi, the official said requesting anonymity.
The US and India have a very consequential relationship, which apart from trade, draws strengths from economic, political and security imperatives, they said, asking not to be named.
The two countries issued a joint statement on February 7 outlining a framework for an interim BTA.
In September, US Ambassador Sergio Gor said India and the United States were working to build a “fair, reciprocal and mutually beneficial” trade relationship.
Pick any sector and the United States and India are working together on it,” Gor said at the 66th annual session of the Automotive Component Manufacturers Association (ACMA) in New Delhi.

items.title: Cheating case accused alleges custodial torture, OU police deny allegations
points: A 31-year-old man’s allegations that he was picked up from Delhi and flown in to Hyderabad before being subjected to torture inside Osmania University police station in a cheating case raised questions about the investigative procedures adopted by…
While Thumma Aditya charged that he was beaten black and blue inside the police station, the OU police flatly denied the same, maintaining that they did not violate any provision of law.
Aditya maintained that a team of policemen, led by Sub-Inspector Karunakar, and accompanied by a civilian Venugopal, turned up at his rented place in Noida on the evening of November 5.
“No papers were shown for the reasons, and no seizure memo formalities were followed,” said Chilla Ramesh, a practicing advocate of Telangana High Court.
“The ‘accused’ was driven to Telangana Bhavan in New Delhi, where he was chained to a bed in a room.
They reached OU police station by 6 a.m. on November 6.

items.title: Rubico targets five-ship MR fleet with latest Top Ships newbuild swoop
points: Nasdaq-listed Rubico has struck a deal to take another two MR tanker newbuildings from Top Ships in a $14.5m deal, continuing the reshuffle of Evangelos Pistiolis-linked tanker orders in China.
The Athens-based owner is buying two special-purpose companies holding shipbuilding contracts for 47,499 dwt product and chemical tankers at Guangzhou Shipyard International (GSI).
Both ships have already secured seven-year time charters with Trafigura Maritime Logistics from delivery, with options for a further four years.
The acquisition would take Rubico’s MR newbuilding pipeline to five vessels, with potential charter revenue of approximately $377.1m.
The vessels also come with sale-and-leaseback financing arranged with a major Chinese leasing house, covering 85% of the shipbuilding instalments at term SOFR plus 1.8%.
The latest move adds to a series of deals between Rubico and Pistiolis-led Top Ships this year.
Rubico was spun off from Top Ships in August 2025 with two 157,000 dwt suezmax tankers, Eco Malibu and Eco West Coast.

items.title: National Conference plans advisory councils of MLAs to address internal dissent
points: To address internal dissent in the party, ruling National Conference (NC) president Dr. Farooq Abdullah on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) started reaching out to party legislators, offering them places in advisory councils that will work with Ministers.
An NC leader, on the condition of anonymity, confirmed to The Hindu that Mr. Abdullah, who chaired a meeting of 17 dissenting legislators on November 6, has decided to constitute the councils.
The NC has 42 legislators in the 90-member Assembly, while the Omar Abdullah government is also supported by four Independent MLAs.
Party sources said the mandate of these advisory councils will be to hold “regular meetings with Ministers on policy decisions and to take stock of the functioning of the departments”.
The move seems to be aimed at addressing the concerns within the party that Chief Minister Omar Abdullah is surrounded by only a small group of individuals.

items.title: Marvel Rivals Debuts Season 11 Trailer With Nightcrawler and Dracula Confirmed
points: NetEase has released a new trailer for Marvel Rivals Season 11, titled Doomsday, launching November 13, 2026, with Nightcrawler joining the playable roster.
The trailer continues the story beyond Season 10.5, with Dr. Doom playing a central role and Dracula set to join as a playable character later in Season 11.5.
The Marvel Rivals Season 11: Doomsday trailer, which debuted on November 10, features an Incursion between two timelines, New York and Nueva York, with two versions of Dr. Doom fighting for survival.
Furthermore, NetEase teases Dracula’s role as the second playable character in Season 11.5 at the end of the trailer.
According to popular Marvel Rivals dataminer X0XLEAK on X, Kurt Wagner, a.k.a.
Nightcrawler, will be a Strategist, while Dracula will be a Vanguard, joining Season 11.
Speaking of Path to Doomsday, Nightcrawler was originally expected to join Marvel Rivals in Season 10.5, but NetEase’s focus on MCU-related events pushed his debut to Season 11.

items.title: Ladakh announces hill council elections, but fails to assuage protesting civil society groups
points: “Elections to all eight Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDCs), covering 100 constituencies across Ladakh, will be held on December 4.

Following the creation of eight districts from the erstwhile two districts of Kargil and Leh, the number of LAHDC constituencies has increased from 26 each in Leh and Kargil to 100 for whole Ladakh,” Ladakh Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra said.
He said November 17 was the last date for filing nominations, November 18 for scrutiny, and November 20 for the withdrawal of candidature.
The Ladakh Chief Secretary said that out of 192 panchayat halqas, 55 sarpanches have been elected unopposed, while elections will be held for the remaining 137 seats.
In the Leh Municipal Council, elections will be held in all 21 wards, while four of the 17 wards in the Kargil Municipal Council have elected their representatives unopposed.

items.title: CM directs officials to strengthen arguments in Supreme Court on Krishna waters
points: Revanth Reddy directed officials to make effective submissions in the Supreme Court to secure Telangana’s rightful share of Krishna River waters and present all necessary evidence on the issues in dispute with Andhra Pradesh.

With the case expected to come up for hearing in the Supreme Court after November 18, the Chief Minister held a review meeting with legal experts and senior irrigation officials on the State’s arguments.

The Chief Minister stressed the need for a strong legal approach to the Krishna water-sharing dispute and asked officials to ensure that all relevant material and evidence were placed before the court.
He also directed engineers to expedite the Dindi and Achampet lift irrigation schemes and reiterated that water for both projects should be supplied from Edula, as decided earlier.
He asked officials to ensure that the required 0.6 tmc ft of water was released from Narlapur to Edula without any hindrance.

items.title: No Global Net Zero Without India': Economist Nicki Hutley To NDTV At COP31
points: As the 31st UN Climate Change Conference takes place in Antalya, Türkiye, one question hangs over the negotiating rooms: energy transition in the world's most populous country.

For Nicki Hutley, an Australian economist who has authored a paper titled 'World's Net Zero Cannot be Complete without India's Net Zero', the answer starts with a simple premise - whether India meets its climate targets is not India's concern alone, she…
In a conversation with NDTV's Gaurie Dwivedi, she set out why the developed world should see India's climate needs as an opportunity rather than a burden.
NITI Aayog's study, released in February, estimates that India needs $22.7 trillion in cumulative investment to reach net zero by 2070.
Even with reforms, the country can mobilise about $16.2 trillion.
That leaves a gap of roughly $6.5 trillion.
By her estimate, about 60% of India's funding needs will have to come from international sources.

items.title: Telangana to host Bharat Summit on November 13 and 14
points: Congress Party Leaders Salman Khurshid, D.

Announcing the event at a press conference here on Tuesday, the chairman of the Congress party’s Foreign Affairs Department, Mr. Salman Khurshid, said the deliberations would focus on democracy, social and economic justice, climate change, gender equality,…
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and party general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have been invited to attend, he said.

The summit will also discuss the implications of artificial intelligence, cloud capitalism and challenges to democratic institutions, as well as explore greater cooperation between countries of the Global North and Global South.

Telangana Minister Sridhar Babu said special sessions under the theme ‘Telangana Rising’ would showcase the State’s development initiatives and discuss urbanisation, welfare, federalism, culture and youth affairs.

Congress Working Committee member Gurdeep Sappal said the idea of an international think-tank involving progressive political parties had emerged during Mr Gandhi’s visit to Germany last year, against the backdrop of a changing global order.

items.title: Tanker Carrying Russian Diesel Halts off U.S. Coast, Shipping Data Shows
points: OSLO, Nov 10 (Reuters) – A tanker carrying the first cargo of Russian diesel for the United States has come to a halt off the US east coast, shipping data showed on Tuesday, with its operator saying its destination had not yet been decided.
President Donald Trump last month announced a surprise deal with Moscow to import diesel from Russia to help lower prices at the pumps ahead of this month’s US midterm elections.

The Malta-flagged tanker Agioi Fanendes was loaded with 40,000 metric tons of ultra-low sulfur diesel in Russia’s Baltic port of Primorsk on October 22, LSEG shipping data showed, with an expected delivery date of November 7.

But the Greece-based company which manages Agioi Fanendes, Eastmed, said a week later that the vessel was proceeding awaiting orders and that a port of discharge had not yet been nominated or finalized.
“Nothing has changed regarding the vessel’s destination, she is still awaiting orders,” Greece-based vessel manager Eastmed told Reuters on Tuesday.

items.title: Shipping heavyweights back Cetus $175m Oslo listing
points: Hong Kong-based dry bulk owner Cetus Maritime has lined up some of shipping’s biggest investment names for a $175m private placement ahead of its planned Oslo listing later this month.
The Mark Young-led company is looking to issue about 95.6m new shares at $1.83 apiece, with an option to increase the placement by another $25m.
The pricing values Cetus at around $239m before the fundraising and its planned fleet acquisition.
The company is targeting its first day of trading on Euronext Growth Oslo around November 18.

The move follows Cetus’s agreement to expand its fleet through a transaction with Hong Kong-listed Seacon Shipping Group, covering 13 handysize and ultramax bulkers, alongside the acquisition of Syngrace, which holds shipbuilding contracts for three…
The latest transaction terms call for approximately $72.5m in cash and the issue of 37.3m Cetus shares.

items.title: Onus on Uttar Pradesh to ensure undertrials allowed bail are released, says Supreme Court
points: Sundresh. | Photo Credit: PTI The Supreme Court has said the onus rests on Uttar Pradesh to ensure that undertrial prisoners granted bail do not continue to languish in jail due to their inability to meet the conditions of their release, such as furnishing…

Sundresh on learning that of the 264 undertrial prisoners who were allowed bail in just 20 of the 75 districts in the nation’s most populous State, only 158 could be released after satisfying the bail conditions imposed by trial courts.
Senior advocate Gaurav Aggarwal, the court’s amicus curiae, submitted that this was the situation in only 20 districts.
Statistics from the other 55 districts of Uttar Pradesh on undertrial prisoners forced to stay back in jails due to their impoverishment were yet unknown.
The court had earlier tasked the District Legal Services Authorities in Uttar Pradesh to reach out to these prisoners and provide them legal aid.

items.title: ADNOC Vessel Damaged in Gulf Attack as UKMTO Reports Fresh Tanker Strike Near Hormuz
points: FILE PHOTO: People walk past a logo of Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) during the annual energy industry event Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference (ADIPEC) in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, November 3, 2025.
ADNOC Logistics & Services confirmed that one of its vessels sustained damage in an attack in the Persian Gulf on the afternoon of November 10.

The announcement came as the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that a tanker had been struck by an unidentified projectile approximately 19 nautical miles northeast of Lima, Oman, near the strategically important Strait of Hormuz.
According to UKMTO Warning 201-26, the incident occurred at 1338 UTC on November 10.
Another tanker transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was reportedly struck by an unidentified projectile on November 7.
In its November 8 advisory, the Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) maintained the threat level for the Strait of Hormuz at SEVERE, warning that further deliberate attacks were highly likely.

items.title: Dipke gets exemption from in-person appearance before magistrate on medical grounds
points: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has been granted an exemption from appearing in-person before the special executive magistrate (SEM) regarding the preventive inquiry against him.
The SEM at Mandir Marg police station allowed the exemption on Tuesday after Dipke’s counsel, Abhik Chimni, cited medical grounds for his absence.
The matter has been posted for December 2 for further proceedings.

During the proceedings, Chimni was also provided copies of the “kalandra” (preventive police report) and other legal documents that the Delhi Police relied on to issue Dipke a show-cause notice, asking him to furnish a bond for maintaining peace.
Dipke was detained on October 16 while heading towards Connaught Place for a protest march called by the CJP under the banner of ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’.
The march was called despite a Delhi Police notice asking him not to participate, citing prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).
He was subsequently arrested on October 17 for allegedly violating a peace bond furnished on October 10.

items.title: Three persons convicted in ₹26.58-lakh commercial tax fraud case in Keralam
points: Enquiry Commissioner and Special Judge (Vigilance) Manoj A. pronounced the verdict against former junior superintendent L.

Pushparani, 58, and Satheesh Kumar, 47, who allegedly acted as an intermediary between traders and officials, to 32 years of rigorous imprisonment each and imposed a fine of ₹11,36,193 on each of them.
Francis, 66, a trader, was sentenced to eight years of rigorous imprisonment and fined ₹6,11,560.
According to the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB), the case relates to irregularities in the payment of advance tax by traders engaged in interstate commerce during 2007-08.
The accused allegedly conspired to use forged challans in which amounts higher than those actually paid into the Treasury were entered in duplicate and triplicate copies.
Pushparani, who was responsible for verifying and confirming the tax amounts remitted to the Treasury, allegedly facilitated the irregularities.
The Vigilance alleged that the manipulation of the challans enabled four business establishments to evade tax, resulting in a total loss of ₹26,58,595 to the government.

items.title: APSCHE to launch digital platform to offer quality online education to students, faculty

Vijayabhaskar Rao will launch a state-wide digital learning initiative, APSCHE LMS–MOOCs, on the occasion of National Education Day on Wednesday (November 11), marking a significant step towards expanding access to quality online education for students and…
The initiative aims to strengthen digital learning, blended education, faculty development and technology-enabled higher education.

The platform will enable students to register, explore courses, enrol in relevant Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), access digital learning materials, participate in assessments and monitor their academic progress.

Speaking at a regional workshop on All-India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE) here on Tuesday, Mr. Rao emphasised the importance of transparency, accuracy and completeness in submitting the data for the academic year 2025-26.
The workshop was organised by the council, in collaboration with the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India.

items.title: Abhiram murder: personal enmity behind the crime, says prime accused
points: Published - November 10, 2026 10:23 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The prime accused, a 17-year-old boy, in the murder of Abhiram in Pangappara has maintained that personal enmity was the motive behind the crime.

The juvenile, who was taken into police custody for evidence collection, reportedly told the investigators that Abhiram’s friend was in a relationship with his former girlfriend, and that he resented the circulation of their photographs and videos on…
He allegedly intended to kill both Abhiram and his friend.
For this, he allegedly planned to use Abhiram to bring the latter to the isolated location where the crime had taken place.

The confession apparently coincided with the emergence of CCTV footage showing scenes prior to the murder, in which Abhiram is seen accompanying the prime accused along a pathway near the crime scene.
During evidence collection and questioning at the crime scene, the prime accused purportedly confessed to taking Abhiram to the secluded area.

points: School Education Minister Rajmohan on Tuesday said discussions are on to establish a committee to purchase books for libraries in a transparent manner.

points: “Extradition of former Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina is a legal matter and it will be dealt with accordingly,” said Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal in response to a question about Ms. Hasina’s presence in India.

He described the passport’s requirement for extradition as a “technical issue” and said, “Obviously, for the travel of people, you need a travel document.” Officials said Ms. Hasina can be extradited either on a Bangladeshi passport or an Emergency…

items.title: Government Has Wide Power To Retire Employees In Public Interest: Supreme Court
points: The government has wide powers to compulsorily retire employees in public interest, the Supreme Court has maintained, observing that such decisions can be taken to ensure administrative efficiency and weed out employees whose continued retention is not…
The court said the assessment of an employee's utility, integrity, efficiency and overall service record is an exercise undertaken by the competent authority.
An employee cannot challenge compulsory retirement merely by arguing that another government servant with a comparable service record was allowed to continue.
"If a wrong has been committed in an earlier case, it cannot be relied upon to perpetuate a similar wrong in subsequent cases," the court said.
A screening committee had assessed 14 employees and recommended five for dismissal.

The assessment involved examining several factors, including honesty, integrity, physical fitness, reputation, efficiency and the employees' overall service records, particularly their Annual Confidential Reports.

items.title: Vande Mataram Row Escalates In Kerala, BJP Targets Kasaragod Collector
points: The BJP has particularly targeted Kasaragod District Collector Sreedhanya Suresh, an IAS officer, accusing her of violating national protocol by sitting down after the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram while the remaining stanzas were still being sung.
The incident occurred during the inauguration of a laboratory at the Muliyar Family Health Centre in Kasaragod.
Video footage shows Minister K Muraleedharan, MP Rajmohan Unnithan, MLA K Mahin and the District Collector taking their seats after the first two stanzas.
Defending his actions, Minister K Muraleedharan maintained that Vande Mataram was never mentioned in the official programme schedule.
He said the programme only listed an Ishwara Prarthana, or invocation song, and there was no prior indication that the complete version of Vande Mataram would be performed.
The BJP maintained that the national song must be accorded due respect and cited the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act while demanding action against the Collector.

items.title: AAP Block Samiti Member Allegedly Shoots Brother Dead In Amritsar Village
points: An alleged family dispute turned fatal in Amritsar's Pandori Waraich village when a Block Samiti member, linked to Aam Aadmi Party, allegedly gunned down his younger brother, triggering widespread tension in the area.
The victim, identified as Simardeep Singh alias Prince, was shot twice - once in the head and once on the right side of his chest.
Upon receiving the information, police rushed to the scene and registered a case against the accused, Karamjit Singh Kammy.
DSP Yadvinder Singh confirmed to the media that police were alerted immediately after the shooting.
Initial probe revealed that the confrontation between the two brothers may have been triggered by a longstanding dispute over the division of family land.
According to locals, the victim was also allegedly involved in drug peddling and abuse, which had reportedly led to frequent tensions within the family.
However, the police are yet to establish the exact motive behind the murder.

points: The government is understood to be considering a distinction between minor events intended to encourage students’ sporting, artistic and cultural talents and large gatherings that interfere with academic activities.

items.title: Patna Municipal Corporation lists Bihar’s first municipal bond on NSE
points: Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC) has listed Bihar’s first-ever municipal bond on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), raising ₹199.99 crore for urban infrastructure projects in the Sate.
The funds raised will be used to finance 15 projects aimed at redeveloping market areas and improving civic services across the city.
The issue, which had a base size of ₹100.03 crore and a greenshoe option of ₹99.96 crore, received investor interest at nearly twice its base issue size.
The bonds carry a coupon rate of 9.20 per cent and are rated AA (Stable) by rating agencies.
Municipal bond issuances have gathered pace in 2026, reflecting growing efforts by urban local bodies to diversify funding sources for infrastructure development.
Among the key issuances this year were Tiruppur City Municipal Corporation’s ₹100 crore bond issue and Coimbatore City Municipal Corporation’s ₹150.85 crore issuance in January 2026.

This was followed by Tiruchirappalli City Municipal Corporation’s ₹100 crore bond issue in February 2026 and Nashik Municipal Corporation’s ₹200 crore fundraising through municipal bonds in March 2026.

items.title: SS United States Sinking Moved Up to Wednesday Due to Weather Concerns
points: The historic SS United States will be sunk off Florida’s Gulf Coast a day earlier than planned after forecasts of heavy winds forced officials to move up the operation.
Okaloosa County announced Monday that the 990-foot ocean liner will be deployed as the world’s largest artificial reef on Wednesday, November 11, instead of Thursday, November 12.
Deployment operations are now scheduled to begin at 1 p.m.
The change comes as the legendary ocean liner makes its final voyage from Mobile, Alabama, to a designated reef site approximately 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin-Fort Walton Beach.
However, a public viewing party will still take place at AJ’s Seafood and Oyster Bar in Destin beginning at noon Wednesday.
Built in 1952, the SS United States still holds the record for the fastest transatlantic crossing by an ocean liner.
The sinking will mark the end of the ship’s 74-year history above water and the beginning of a new role as a diving destination and marine habitat off Florida’s Emerald Coast.

Gollagunta will become Executive Vice-President and Head of Corporate Development.
He will work from Mahindra's Worli office in Mumbai and report directly to Group CEO and Managing Director Dr Anish Shah.

Gollagunta joined Mahindra in April 2023 and took charge as CEO of its automotive division at a time when the company was building on the success of the Scorpio-N, Thar and XUV700 while preparing a much larger electric SUV push.

Anish Shah has said Mahindra will enter a new area only if it has a genuine advantage over competitors, can build the business to a meaningful size and can earn returns better than the industry average.
In the July-September 2026 quarter, its automotive business reported a 55% increase in consolidated profit after tax.
Across the wider group, consolidated revenue rose 25% to Rs 57,553 crore, while profit after tax increased 25% to Rs 4,588 crore.

items.title: "Fabricated, Malicious": India Rejects Khalistani Terrorist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's US Lawsuit
points: New Delhi's response came after the US State Department confirmed that it had formally transmitted court-issued summonses to the Indian government through diplomatic channels.
External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said today that India strongly rejected the allegations directed at its senior officials as well as the lawsuit itself.
"We reject the fabricated and malicious attacks on our high officials.
A request for serving of judicial documents in India can only be routed through India's designated central authority that is the Ministry of Law and Justice," Jaiswal said.

According to the US State Department, the documents were transmitted to the Indian Embassy in Washington DC through diplomatic channels on October 9, following the signing of a diplomatic note on September 30, 2026.
The civil lawsuit was filed by Pannun, who serves as legal counsel for Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), a separatist organisation banned in India.

items.title: Assam Cabinet Approves Rs 108 Crore For College Fee Waiver, Hikes Ex-Gratia For Samagra Shiksha Employees
points: The Assam government has approved Rs 108 crore to reimburse colleges and universities under its admission fee waiver scheme, while increasing the financial assistance for families of deceased Samagra Shiksha employees from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 7.5 lakh.

Among other key proposals cleared were a collaboration with IIT Guwahati's Research Park to develop teaching materials for primary school students and the merger of Krishna Kanta Handiqui Sanskrit College in Guwahati with Bhaskar Varman Sanskrit University…
The Rs 108-crore allocation will be used to compensate educational institutions for admission fees waived for students belonging to families below the prescribed income limit.
The assistance has been increased to Rs 7.5 lakh from the existing Rs 5 lakh, as proposed in the state Budget.
On healthcare coverage, the government approved Rs 2 crore towards its share under the Ayushman Bharat-linked scheme.

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the Centre's assistance covers approximately 30 lakh families, while the Assam government bears the cost of healthcare coverage for around 40 lakh additional families.
